entries.heading: The one rule
entries.body: Every working set goes to failure or one rep short. Your load stays fixed for weeks at a time, so effort is your only variable. Light loads taken to failure grow muscle as well as heavy ones (7.8% vs 8.1% CSA in Lasevicius et al.). Light loads stopped short grow almost nothing (2.8%).

entries.heading: Beat reps, not weight
entries.body: The number under each set is what you did last time. That's your target. Set the weight to something you can genuinely take to failure. If the prescribed number isn't that, change it on the home screen. Reps at a weight you can't finish aren't a measurement of anything.

entries.heading: Why B is shaped like this
entries.body: B is the side delt and chest day; A carries the compounds. Every set is now paired with something that does not compete with it, so the lateral raise gets about 115 seconds between rounds instead of 65 — with less total rest than before. The old note here claimed 20 sets a week is where extra volume stops paying. It isn't: the curve flattens, it never turns off.

entries.heading: Seven reps is not a loss
entries.body: B used to ask for 15–25 on a lateral raise you can do eight of. Every set read as a failure and you stopped doing it. Load doesn't decide growth once a set goes to failure — 40, 60 and 80% of 1RM grew the same in Lasevicius 2018, and 28 studies agree. The targets now match what you actually do, so beating one means something.

entries.heading: Progression ladder
entries.body: 1. Add reps.  2. Slow the eccentric to 4–5s and add a 2s pause in the stretch.  3. Add post-failure partials in the bottom third.  4. Go up a notch in weight. The trigger is written into the set itself: 15 reps on the first lateral raise and another 1.25 kg goes on each handle, reps restarting from a fresh baseline.  5. Switch to a no-ceiling variant: pike push-ups, Z-press, archer push-ups, chin-ups.

entries.heading: Protein: 120 g/day
entries.body: 2.0 g/kg, roughly 30 g across four meals. Make one of them within a couple of hours of finishing. Anywhere in 105–140 g is fine.

entries.heading: Calories: +250/day
entries.body: You're lean and already burning through cycling and yoga. Target +150–250 g on the scale per week. If the weekly average is flat, eat more. This is the bottleneck, not the training.

entries.heading: Creatine: 5 g/day
entries.body: Any time of day, no loading needed. The only supplement worth the money. Expect +1–1.5 kg in the first fortnight from intracellular water. That's fullness, not fat.

entries.heading: Fasted is fine
entries.body: Total daily intake beats timing. Don't rebuild your morning around a pre-workout meal. A coffee 20 minutes before does more for this session than food will.

entries.heading: The two ways this fails
entries.body: ① You don't go to failure, because 5 or 10 kg doesn't feel like it deserves that much effort.  ② You don't eat more.
